Currently, Mexican exports of vehicles and parts to the EU face an average tariff of approximately 10%. The new agreement explicitly includes these sectors to reflect the current industrial landscape. Rosendo Gutiérrez, Mexico’s Deputy Secretary of Foreign Trade, said the removal of these duties will boost bilateral automotive trade and provide greater legal certainty for long-term investments. “Mexico wants to reduce its dependence on its northern neighbor, but also on Asian, or rather Chinese, supply chains, and in Europe we are pursuing the same objectives,” an EU official said on condition of anonymity. results.title: EV rules of origin, CAM, and why tariffs still don't bite
results.content:
In late December, Jamieson Greer reported to the House Ways and Means and Senate Finance Committees on the US approach to the upcoming USMCA joint review. The report sets out a (fairly punchy) list of issues Mexico and Canada will be expected to address. A selection:

 Mexican policies that promote the use of third-country content and erode U.S.

  supply chains;
 Unfair granting of protection for numerous meat and cheese terms to the [...] European Union, which threatens market access for U.S. producers [Mexico]
 Longstanding concerns with the methodology Mexico applies to calculate an

  annual spectrum use fee
 Equal treatment for U.S. electronic payment service suppliers so they can

  process domestic transactions using their own proprietary networks as

  Mexico committed to under the USMCA
 The impact of Canada’s Online Streaming and Online News Acts for U.S. [...] And, as long time readers of MFN will know, nothing gets me more excited than electric vehicle rules of origin.

At its core, the issue is simple: electric vehicles traded between the EU and UK currently qualify for tariff-free trade thanks to a rules of origin derogation, which allows them to use a higher proportion of foreign content and, crucially, foreign batteries.

After already being extended once, this derogation is set to expire at the end of 2026.
